q: Explain the phylloxera status of Santorini and Nemea's vine-training contrast.
accept: santorini ungrafted volcanic ash nemea grafted
ash prevents phylloxera
ans: Santorini's ash is phylloxera-hostile — vines are own-rooted and centuries old, renewed by layering; mainland Nemea grafts normally

q: Explain how Tokaj's vineyard classification of 1700–1737 worked.
accept: first second third class vineyards rakoczi survey soil aspect
classified into classes by quality
ans: Vineyards were graded into classes (first, second, third) on soil, aspect and proven quality — a Rákóczi-era survey formalized by royal decree in 1737
exp: Predating both the 1855 Médoc and Burgundy's formal climat rankings.

q: Explain the economics that nearly destroyed Tokaj in the 20th century.
accept: communist state farms bulk production quality collapse until 1990s investment
collectivization destroyed quality
ans: Collectivization replaced selective aszú picking with bulk state production; quality collapsed until foreign and domestic investment rebuilt it after 1989
exp: The 1990s privatization is why the modern names are so recent.

q: Argue Assyrtiko's case as a great white grape, with three pieces of evidence.
accept: acid retention in heat age worthiness ungrafted ancient vines saline minerality
holds acid ages ancient vines
ans: It holds searing acid at high sugar in near-desert heat; it ages a decade-plus; and it grows on ungrafted centuries-old vines in volcanic ash — structure, longevity and provenance in one variety
exp: Three-pillar arguments are the oral's favourite structure.

q: Walk through how Tokaji Aszú is made and aged under the rules in force today.
accept: aszu berries are macerated in must or base wine then pressed with a minimum 120 grams of sugar and 18 months in oak
individually picked aszu berries soaked in base wine pressed and aged at least 18 months before a third year release
the 2013 reform set 120 g/l minimum and abolished three and four puttonyos
berry by berry selection maceration pressing slow fermentation and barrel ageing in tokaj
ans: Botrytised aszú berries are picked individually over repeated passes through the vineyard and collected as a paste. That paste is macerated in must or in finished base wine - traditionally somewhere between twelve and sixty hours, longer for more extraction - and then pressed; the resulting sweet must ferments very slowly and often stops of its own accord well short of dryness. The 2013 reform fixed the modern standard: a minimum of 120 g/L residual sugar for all Aszú, which is the old five-puttonyos level; at least 18 months in oak; and no release before 1 January of the third year after the harvest. Three and four puttonyos were abolished, as was the Aszúeszencia category. Where 'puttonyos' still appears it is optional and can only be 5 or 6. Eszencia, the free-run nectar, remains separate and is not Aszú at all.
exp: This is the clearest case in the bank of law diverging from textbook: the puttony is now a label tradition rather than the measure, and any answer built on three and four puttonyos is describing a system that no longer exists. Note also that the wood minimum came down - from two years to eighteen months - deliberately, to allow fresher, less oxidative styles.

q: Trace the rise of dry Furmint in Tokaj and explain what it demanded of growers.
accept: szepsy and mad led the dry furmint movement from the late 1990s using clean pre-botrytis fruit
dry furmint required healthy fruit picked before botrytis lower yields and revived the single vineyard dulo names
a modern movement centred on mad that put the historic vineyard classification to work on dry wine
post 1989 producers turned furmint into a dry single vineyard white
ans: Dry Furmint always existed in Tokaj, but as a by-product and a peasant's drink. The modern movement dates from the late 1990s and 2000s, with István Szepsy the central figure and the village of Mád its epicentre - Királyudvar, Barta, Demeter Zoltán, Gizella, Holdvölgy and the Tokaj Renaissance association alongside him. It demanded an entirely different vineyard discipline: healthy, clean fruit picked before botrytis rather than after it, severe yield reduction to get concentration without sugar accumulation from noble rot, and the abandonment of the aszú economics that let growers pick over the same rows repeatedly. Winemaking moved to large old wood, acacia or steel, with texture from lees rather than from oak flavour. Crucially, the dry wines revived the dűlő - single vineyards such as Szent Tamás, Betsek, Nyulászó, Király and Úrágya - putting the eighteenth-century classification back to work on a wine it was never written for. The style is high in acid, smoky, saline and unmistakably volcanic.
exp: The commercial logic matters as much as the aesthetic one: the world market for very sweet wine shrank, and dry Furmint gave Tokaj a wine to sell in volume while keeping the vineyard names alive. It is also why the region's site classification survived at all.

q: Compare Xinomavro as it is expressed in Naoussa, Amyndeon and Goumenissa.
accept: naoussa is pure xinomavro and the most structured amyndeon is high cold and sandy goumenissa blends negoska
naoussa full and tannic amyndeon lighter and permitted for rose and sparkling goumenissa softened with negoska
three northern greek pdos for xinomavro with negoska only in the goumenissa blend
same grape three appellations differing by altitude soil and blending partner
ans: Naoussa is the benchmark and is monovarietal Xinomavro, grown on the south-east facing slopes of Mount Vermio at roughly 150 to 400 metres - warmer than Amyndeon, and the fullest, most tannic, longest-lived and most classically Nebbiolo-like of the three, all dried tomato, olive and dried flowers over ferocious tannin. Amyndeon sits on the plateau on the other side of Vermio, at roughly 570 to 750 metres, distinctly colder, with sandy soils in which some ungrafted vines survived phylloxera; the wines are paler, higher-toned, more red-fruited and earlier-drinking, and it is the only Greek PDO that permits still and sparkling rosé Xinomavro. Goumenissa, on the slopes of Mount Paiko from about 150 metres up, is the blend: Xinomavro with a minimum 20% Negoska - the familiar 80/20 formula - Negoska being a fleshier, lower-acid, softer-tannin variety that fills the middle palate and rounds the finish. Same grape, three answers - structure in Naoussa, aromatics and lift in Amyndeon, flesh in Goumenissa.
exp: Xinomavro's name means 'acid black', and every one of these zones is a different strategy for managing that. If a blind glass shows the Nebbiolo signature with unexpected softness, Goumenissa is the answer the room is waiting for; if it shows the signature at rosé weight, think Amyndeon - the one PDO where sparkling and still rosé Xinomavro are legal, Zitsa (from Debina) being Greece's other sparkling appellation.

q: Explain PDO Santorini's permitted styles, and what Nykteri means both legally and practically.
accept: dry white built on at least 85 percent assyrtiko plus vinsanto and nykteri is the riper barrel aged style
nykteri means night work and is a legally defined richer oaked santorini at higher alcohol
santorini pdo is assyrtiko led with aidani and athiri and nykteri is its barrel aged designation
the pdo covers dry assyrtiko sweet vinsanto and the nykteri style
ans: PDO Santorini covers dry white built on a minimum of 85% Assyrtiko - raised from 75% by the 2022 amendment - with Athiri and Aidani permitted for the balance, and the sun-dried sweet Vinsanto, which needs at least 51% Assyrtiko alongside Aidani, Athiri and a handful of minor island varieties, is dried to at least 370 g/L of sugar and given a minimum of two years' oxidative maturation. Nykteri is a third, legally defined designation within the PDO rather than a producer's fancy: the same 85% Assyrtiko base, a minimum of 13.5% alcohol and at least three months in oak, made from riper fruit and therefore fuller, waxier, broader and more textural than a straight Santorini, though the acid remains. The name means working through the night - grapes were picked at first light and pressed and vinified in darkness to keep them cool on an island that had neither shade nor refrigeration. So Nykteri is where Santorini officially embraces both oak and ripeness, which is exactly the combination the appellation's reputation is otherwise built on refusing.
exp: Candidates almost always know Assyrtiko and kouloura and stop there. Knowing that the PDO carries three defined styles - and that one of them mandates barrel - is the difference between a memorised fact and a working knowledge of the appellation. Watch the moving figure: older texts still print 75% Assyrtiko for the dry wine, and the current minimum is 85%.

montosoli north castelnuovo dell'abate south
ans: North (cooler, galestro; Altesino and Caparzo on Montosoli, Canalicchio) vs south (warmer, clay-limestone; Castelnuovo dell'Abate — Mastrojanni, Poggio di Sotto). Biondi-Santi's Il Greppo lies south-east of the town at roughly 500 m — cooled by altitude, not latitude
exp: Soldera's Case Basse sat southwest — its own weather system entirely.

q: Explain the Super Tuscan legal arc from 1970s IGT exile to today.
accept: vino da tavola then igt toscana 1992 goria law bolgheri doc 1994
tavola to igt to doc
ans: Bordeaux-variety wines sold as humble Vino da Tavola → the 1992 Goria law created IGT → Bolgheri DOC (created 1983 for bianco and rosato only, rewritten in 1994 to admit the Bordeaux reds as Bolgheri Rosso/Superiore) and the standalone Bolgheri Sassicaia DOC (2013) legitimized them
exp: The rebellion was absorbed by the system it embarrassed.

q: Which Tuscan coastal DOC did Ornellaia and Masseto put on the map, and what distinguishes Masseto's site?
accept: bolgheri masseto blue clay merlot
bolgheri clay hill pure merlot
ans: Bolgheri; Masseto's hillside blue clay (Pliocene) grows pure Merlot — Italy's Pétrus analogue
exp: Masseto has been a standalone estate with its own cellar since 2018, but the wine is still Toscana IGT — it never gained an appellation of its own.
